significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds for every n ≥ 4. The even case is Davis and Kohl's own Corollary 3.14; the new case is odd n ≥ 5, where the stable set polytope of the complement of the odd cycle is not a lattice-point-friendly compressed polytope and has the extra rank facet. The proof counts the lattice points of the dilates directly from the known facet description of the antihole (Padberg): a greedy recursion around the cycle has a unique real cyclic fixed point; expanding the integer residual weights counts matchings of the cycle, which gives the perfectly matchable set polynomial, and the half-integral fixed points give the one extra monomial z^{(n+1)/2}; a rank-2 transfer matrix assembles the generating function. Lean proves the identity for all n ≥ 4, odd and even, from the lattice-point description of the dilated polytope, so it does not depend on the source's Corollary 3.14, and checks the source's Table 2 for n = 4..7.
significance.caveat: The new contribution is odd n ≥ 5; even n is Davis and Kohl's Corollary 3.14 (the Lean proof covers both parities independently). The journal version (Discrete Math. 347(7) (2024) 114018, doi 10.1016/j.disc.2024.114018) could not be read: the reviewer's probability that it already proves the odd case is 0.10, so its Section 3.1 should be checked by hand before any unqualified novelty claim. The facet description of the antihole stable set polytope is Padberg's classical theorem, used in the paper; the Lean statement is about the lattice points of the dilates of the polytope given by those inequalities. Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (two rounds; not routine 0.65).
